rows.text: The MA STAR operating instructions (mastar-manual.md, section 7.3 'Checking the Load Nut's Wear Indicator', p. 34) require the load nut's wear indicator to be checked every 6 months, and the nut pair replaced when the wear limit is reached.

The UR10e User Manual, section 17.4 "Long Term Storage" (printed page 212, under the heading "p. 209" in the file), recommends unpacking and starting up robots at least yearly, which is every 12 months.
The nanoScan3 I/O operating instructions (Section 14, Technical Data, performance table) state a mission time TM (ISO 13849) of 20 years for both the Core I/O and Pro I/O variants.

The UR5e User Manual, in the Safety section under 4.3 General Warnings and Cautions (WARNING: HOT SURFACE, manual p. 30 / printed page 33), says to allow the robot to cool down by powering it off and waiting one hour before handling it.

The UNIVPM guideline (Linee guida gestione attrezzature di laboratorio, v1.0, 2024), quoting Article 71, paragraph 9 of D.Lgs. 81/08, says the written results of the checks must be kept available to the supervisory bodies for at least the last three years. The passage is on the page marked p. 5 (footer 'Pagina 3 di 10').

No. The UR10e is delivered as a partly completed machine with an EU Declaration of Incorporation (Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC, Annex II B), not a Declaration of Conformity; the integrator who completes the machine applies the CE mark. The Directive also says the CE marking goes on machinery (Art. 16), and partly completed machinery is covered by Art. 13 and Art. 6(2) rather than a CE conformity marking.
No. The nanoScan3 operating instructions (p. 11, section 2.3 Improper use) list 'Outdoors' under 'Impermissible ambient conditions', so the scanner must not be used outdoors.

Yes. The UR10e manual, section 10.3.3 "Safety Configuration without Teach Pendant" (printed page 126), says the robot can be used without the Teach Pendant attached, but removing it requires defining another Emergency Stop source. The Teach Pendant must be removed from the vicinity of the robot, because its Emergency Stop button stops working once it is detached or disconnected.

rows.text: Apart from the regular thorough check (section 10.2), the nanoScan3 manual requires a thorough check during commissioning and after modifications (section 9.5, p. 105). Section 9.1 (p. 104) specifies that the effectiveness of the protective measure must be checked after each change to the machine, the integration, or the operating and boundary conditions of the scanner.

rows.value: The person/s integrating the UR robot are responsible for the risk assessment of the robot application (for performing a risk assessment for the complete robot system).
rows.text: Section 4.4 'Integration and Responsibility' of the UR10e manual places the risk assessment on the integrator: the person(s) integrating the UR robot must perform a risk assessment for the complete robot system.

The UR10e User Manual (ur10e-manual.md, section 18.2 'Replace the Control box filters', p. 216 of the manual) says there is a filter on either side of the control box and gives the steps for replacing it, but it does not state how often the filters must be replaced. No other document in the folder gives a replacement interval for the UR10e control box filters.

The files do not record the date of the last regular thorough check of the cell's nanoScan3. The nanoScan3 manual (section 5.6.2, 'Planning the regular thorough check') only requires these checks at least once a year. The robot-cell sheet (Scheda 2.4.16), the IGEA equipment list and the university guidelines contain no record of a nanoScan3 check.

The UR5e User Manual (ur5e-manual.md, section 18 'Maintenance and Repair') says maintenance, inspection and calibration must follow the safety instructions and the UR Service Manual, but it gives no recalibration interval. The other documents in the folder do not state one for the UR5e either, so the files do not answer how often it must be recalibrated.

Crane 13 (IGEA-PRIM 5t, a fixed overhead travelling crane built in 2017) falls under Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/2008, row 16: fixed lifting equipment over 200 kg, used in sectors such as extractive (estrattivo), built less than 10 years ago, so it must be verified every two years (biennale). The IGEA technical sheet confirms that all 24 positions follow the Allegato VII intervals.

The DEFRIES-TITANO overhead travelling crane (position 11, GRU A PONTE SCORREVOLE, built 1978, Masua-Acquaresi, Iglesias, an 'Area mineraria') must be verified annually. Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/2008, row 15, sets annual checks for fixed lifting appliances over 200 kg used in extractive sectors that were built more than 10 years ago. The files do not state outright that an overhead travelling crane is 'fisso'; I took that from its listing in the plant records as a non-mobile crane.

The AMCO VEBA crane at position 4 (Tabella A1 of the IGEA record, 520 kg, built 2005, mobile truck-mounted, mining-area use) falls under Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/2008 rows 12 and 14, which both require annual verification (verifica annuale). The IGEA record also states that the verifications follow the Allegato VII schedule.

Under Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/08 (row 14), a mobile lifting appliance over 200 kg used regularly and manufactured more than 10 years ago needs an annual verification. Position 18 (JCB JS190NLC, 7500 kg, built 2010, per IGEA Allegato A, Tabella A4) fits that case, so it would need verification every year.

Assuming the crane is a fixed installation, a regular-use, fixed overhead crane built in 2017 (less than 10 years old) must be verified every three years under Allegato VII, D.Lgs. 81/08, row 18. The files do not expressly classify overhead travelling cranes as fixed or mobile, so this is an inference; if it were treated as mobile, the rule would be biennial (row 13). The crane reaches 10 years in 2027, after which the fixed-crane rule in row 17 gives biennial checks.

The GUTTER overhead travelling crane (position 10, built 1988, 3000 kg, Masua) is a fixed-type lifting appliance older than 10 years used regularly outside the listed sectors, so Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/2008 (row 17) requires verification every two years. This assumes the crane is 'fisso'; if it were classed as mobile or transferable, row 14 would require annual verification.

According to Allegato B, Tabella B3 of the IGEA plant record, two lifting devices are located at Lula (Sos Enattos): position 6 (hydraulic truck crane FASSI on IVECO FIAT) and position 23 (gantry crane, Euro Costruzioni Pellegrini GCB 35 X). Note that the summary in section 2.2 (p. 3) gives a quantity of only 1 for Lula, which conflicts with Tabella B3.

The IGEA technical sheet (Scheda tecnica, section 4 'IMPEGNI AGGIUDICATARIO / VERIFICATORE', page 5) requires the verifier to plan the checks jointly with IGEA's appointed staff and to notify IGEA at least 15 days in advance.

No. Under point 4.2.1 of the IGEA technical sheet, IGEA provides the verifier with the necessary personnel and means (pesi campione), but expressly excludes measuring instruments (apparecchi di misurazione). This is in section 4 'Impegni Appaltatore' on page 4 of igea-equipment.md.

rows.value: The ASL (Aziende Sanitarie Locali) are in charge of the periodic verifications after the first one, and must carry them out within 30 days of the request.
rows.text: Under art. 2, c. 1 of the Decreto Ministeriale 11 aprile 2011 (DM2011), the ASL are responsible for the verifications periodiche successive alla prima, to be carried out within trenta giorni dalla richiesta; the INAIL handles the first verification, within sixty days. The IGEA technical sheet (igea-equipment.md, pp. 3–4) covers these post-first verifications and refers to the DM 11 aprile 2011 for their methods.

Yes. The P&H R200 mobile crane at position 17 (autogru, built 1977, matricola 70761) has been in service for more than 20 years. Under DM 11 aprile 2011, Allegato II, point 3.2.3, the employer must show the results of the supplementary investigations (point 2(c)) during periodic verifications of mobile cranes. The IGEA plant sheet asks for the same thing as a structural verification of residual life for equipment over 20 years old.

The IGEA plant record (igea-equipment.md, Allegato A, Tabella A2, and Allegato B, Tabella B1) identifies position 9 as a DEMAG 5000 overhead travelling crane (matricola 503292, INAIL CA 128/86, built 1985, located at Meccanizzazione in Iglesias). However, the files do not give the date of its last periodic verification: the scheda says the last-verification dates are in the Allegato A tables, but those tables contain no verification-date column or value for position 9.

The files do not record when position 17 (P&H R200, built 1977) was last verified, so they cannot show whether the 14 November 2026 check is overdue. Under Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/08 (DLGSALLVII.md, rows 12 and 14), a mobile lifting appliance over 200 kg built more than 10 years earlier needs annual verification. The IGEA technical sheet (igea-equipment.md, p. 6, Tabella A4) lists the crane but gives no verification date, and its scope covers only 2019–2021.

The IGEA-PRIM 5t overhead travelling crane (position 13, manufactured January 2017, per the IGEA technical sheet Allegato A, table A2) must be verified annually. Under Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/08, lines 12 and 15, lifting equipment over 200 kg used in the extractive sector is verified annually, and the fixed-equipment line applies to units more than 10 years old, which this crane is by 1 June 2027.

In 2028 the IGEA-PRIM 5t bridge crane (position 13, manufactured 2017) is 11 years old, so it falls under the 'fixed, extractive sector, manufactured more than 10 years earlier' row of Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/2008, which requires annual verification. This assumes a bridge crane counts as 'fisso', which the files do not state explicitly.

Position 3 (FASSI F 28 B22, 1500 kg, manufactured 2009) is a mobile lifting appliance over 200 kg. Under regular use and not older than 10 years in 2018, Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/2008 requires verification every two years (biennale), so it would be verified once every two years, not annually. The annual rule applies only to construction, steel, port and extractive use.

Under regular use, a mobile lifting appliance over 200 kg that was built more than 10 years earlier (the FASSI F 28 B22, built 2009, position 3 in IGEA's plant record) must be verified annually, so once in 2024. This comes from Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/2008, row 14, as reproduced in DLGSALLVII.md.

The Effer 790 truck-mounted crane at position 7 (IGEA, Iglesias, 'Area mineraria') is a mobile lifting appliance over 200 kg used in the extractive sector, so Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/2008 (row 12) requires verification every year (annual), which means on 1 June 2029 it falls due once a year. The IGEA schedule also states that verification follows the Allegato VII cadences.

The IGEA-PRIM 5t bridge crane (position 13, Allegato A, Tabella A2; manufactured 2017) would need verification once a year in 2031. Outside the construction, steel, port and extractive sectors, a mobile or transferable lifting appliance over 200 kg that is used regularly and was made more than 10 years earlier falls under Allegato VII, row 14 of D.Lgs. 81/2008, which requires annual verification. The crane was built in 2017, so by 2031 it is 14 years old. This classification assumes the crane counts as mobile or transferable; if it were treated as fixed, row 17 would apply instead, with biennial verification.

The KITO KR50L electric hoist at position 16 (built 2000, capacity 5000 kg) must be verified every year. Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/2008 (DLGSALLVII.md, rows 14 and 15) sets annual verification for non-hand-operated lifting appliances over 200 kg that are more than 10 years old, and for fixed ones used in the extractive sector; the IGEA plant record lists it as a 'paranco elettrico' with year 2000 in Tabella A3.

The GCB 35 gantry crane (position 23, Lula – Sos Enattos mine, built 1989, 35,000 kg) must be verified every year. Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/2008 requires annual verification for lifting equipment over 200 kg used in the extractive sector, and for fixed equipment built more than 10 years earlier. IGEA's technical sheet (Allegato A, table A5) confirms position 23 is in the mine at Lula.

Outside the construction, steel, port and extractive sectors, a mobile or transferable lifting device over 200 kg used regularly and manufactured more than 10 years ago needs verification every year. The SIS PROFI 10 TI (position 14, 10,000 kg, built 2002) falls in that category, so the answer is annual under Allegato VII, row 14 of D.Lgs. 81/08.

According to the IGEA equipment list (Allegato A, Tabelle A2, A4 and A5), positions 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 17 and 23 have a year of construction before 1990 (1985, 1985, 1988, 1978, 1980, 1977 and 1989). Position 15's record reads "declass. 1997" and position 1 is 1991, so neither qualifies.

In the IGEA plant list (igea-equipment.md, Allegato A, Tabella A1, p. 6, and Allegato B, Tabella B1/B2, pp. 8-9), positions 2, 5 and 6 are the only ones with a stated capacity of 995 kg, which is below 1,000 kg. Positions 4 and 7 show no capacity figure, and positions 22 and 24 have numbers that are not clearly capacities, so they are not counted.

In Allegato B (Tabella B1, p. 8 of igea-equipment.md), the word "Monteponi" appears in the location column for positions 13 (IGEA PRIM 5t gru a ponte scorrevole) and 14 (Palair/J.D. Neuhaus paranco pneumatico, Iglesias). The OCR text is garbled, so the sector labels next to these rows ("Pozzo Vittorio" and "Livello Vesme") are not fully clear. Section 2.2 (p. 3) also summarises 19 units in Iglesias under "Area mineraria Monteponi", which would cover more positions than these two.

rows.text: Under section 4.2.2 of the IGEA technical sheet (Scheda tecnica, pages 4-5), IGEA must give the verifier the structural residual-life certification for equipment over 20 years old. As of 14 November 2026, that covers truck-mounted cranes at positions 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6, built in 1991, 2005, 2005, 2003 and 2004 (Allegato A, Tabella A1, page 6). Positions 3 (2009) and 7 (2017) are under 20 years old.
Under Allegato III, punto 4.2 of the Ministerial Decree of 11 April 2011 (DM2011), authorised bodies must keep all documentary records relating to their verification activity for at least ten years.

Position 7 in Table A1 of the IGEA plant record (igea-equipment.md, Allegato A and Allegato B) is an Effer 790 crane on an FIAT truck, matricola 100026789, but the registration plate (targa) cell for that row is blank or holds an INAIL-style code (2018/200045/CA), so the files do not give the plate.

The files do not give a euro amount. Position 23 is the 35,000 kg 'gru a cavalletto' (gantry crane) in IGEA's Allegato A, Tabella A5 (igea-equipment.md, p. 5-6). IGEA's schedule says the fee is calculated from the tariff in the Decreto Dirigenziale of 23/11/2012, with ISTAT indices and the contractor's discount, but that tariff itself is not in the files. INAIL's guide (inail-guide.md, pp. 37-38) likewise refers to that tariff without stating an amount.

Directive 2006/42/EC is repealed with effect from 14 January 2027 (Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Article 51(2)). The transitional rule in Article 52(1) covers only products placed on the market in conformity with the Directive before 14 January 2027. The machine is first made available on 25 January 2027, so the Regulation applies, and the 10 January 2027 declaration date does not change that.

No. On 1 December 2026 Directive 2006/42/EC still applies, since it is repealed only with effect from 14 January 2027 (Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Article 51(2)). For a machine in Annex IV not built to harmonised standards, Article 12(4) of the Directive allows only EC type-examination (Annex IX) plus internal checks (Annex VIII, point 3), or full quality assurance (Annex X). Unit verification (module G) is not among the options.

rows.text: Under Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Article 25(3) and Annex I, Part A, these four categories (all from Directive 2006/42/EC Annex IV points 14, 15, 16 and 18) must use module B+C, H or G, so internal production control (module A) is not available for them even with harmonised standards applied. The Regulation applies from 14 January 2027 (Article 54), so this holds on 1 February 2027. The files contain no 1 December 2026 rule.

rows.value: Manufacturer: the company is considered a 'manufacturer' under Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 and takes the manufacturer's obligations (Article 10) for the modified machinery.
rows.text: From 20 January 2027 (as corrected by the corrigendum), Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies, so on 1 March 2027 it governs the machine. Under its Article 18, a person other than the original manufacturer or a non-professional user who carries out a substantial modification is considered a manufacturer and must meet the manufacturer's obligations under Article 10, including a new conformity assessment.

Yes. Under Article 10(7) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (REG.md), which applies from 14 January 2027 (corrected to 20 January 2027 by CORR.md), instructions for use may be provided in digital format. The manufacturer must mark how to access them, make them printable, downloadable and online for the machine's lifetime and at least 10 years, and supply paper free of charge within one month if the user asks at purchase. The UNIVPM guideline's paper-only statement (section 4, p. 5) relies on Directive 2006/42/EC, which this Regulation repeals from that date (Article 51(2)).

rows.text: On 1 March 2027 Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (the Machinery Regulation) applies, since it applies from 14 January 2027 and repeals Directive 2006/42/EC from that date. Under Article 15(2), before making machinery (not partly completed machinery) available, a distributor must verify the four items listed.

Under Article 52(1) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, as corrected by the Corrigendum to OJ L 169 (4.7.2023), point 6, machines placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC before 20 January 2027 may not be impeded by Member States. The last day for placing on the market is therefore 19 January 2027. The REG.md text still reads 14 January 2027, but the corrigendum replaces that date.

Under Article 54, third paragraph, point (c) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Article 6(7) applies from 13 July 2023 as first printed, but the corrigendum in CORR.md (point 13) changes that date to 19 July 2023. The corrected date is therefore 19 July 2023.

Article 53(3) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 sets the first specific report for 14 July 2026 and then every five years, so the second falls in 2031. The corrigendum in CORR.md changes the first-subparagraph date from 14 July to 20 July, which gives 20 July 2031 as the corrected date (the uncorrected text would give 14 July 2031).

No. Under Article 47(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, the Commission's delegation runs for five years from 13 July 2023, so it ends in July 2028. The report is due no later than nine months before that, around October 2027, so the deadline has not passed as of 14 November 2026.

No. Under Directive 2006/42/EC, a partly completed machine such as the UR10e may not be put into service until the final machinery it is incorporated into has been declared in conformity. The manufacturer's declaration of incorporation must state this (Annex II, part 1, section B, point 6), and Article 5(2) and Article 13(1) require the manufacturer's procedure to be completed before the product is placed on the market.

rows.value: The technical file for the final machinery
rows.text: Under Directive 2006/42/EC, Article 13(2), the assembly instructions and the declaration of incorporation accompany the partly completed machinery until it is incorporated into the final machinery, and then they form part of the technical file for that machinery. The UR5e manual's Declaration of Incorporation and assembly instructions therefore become part of the technical file of the final robot cell.

rows.text: Under Article 5(1) of Directive 2006/42/EC (the Machinery Directive, which still applies on 14 November 2026 because Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies only from 14 January 2027), the manufacturer or its authorised representative must, before placing the machinery on the market and/or putting it into service, complete six steps (a)–(f). The files do not use the word 'integrator'; the integrator is treated as the manufacturer only through the Article 2(i) definition, which the files state for the case where no manufacturer exists, so that link is an inference.

Yes. Directive 2006/42/EC is repealed from 20 January 2027 (Art. 51(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, as corrected by CORR.md), so a unit placed on the market on 1 March 2027 falls under that Regulation. Vehicle servicing lifts are listed in its Annex I, Part A, point 3, which requires a Article 25(2) procedure involving a notified body (module B+C, H or G). Under Article 24(3), the CE marking must therefore be followed by the notified body's identification number. The MA STAR manual's declaration cites only Directive 2006/42/EC and names no notified body, so it does not cover a 2027 unit.

The files do not give a maximum penalty amount for infringing Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 in Italy. Article 50(1) of REG.md (Regulation 2023/1230) only requires Member States to lay down penalties that are effective, proportionate and dissuasive, and Article 50(2) sets a notification deadline of 14 October 2026. No Italian implementing text with a sanction amount is in the folder.

The files do not record the date on which the Commission actually adopted the first implementing act under Article 6(10) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230. REG.md, Article 6(10), only sets the deadline: "The first such implementing act shall be adopted not later than 14 July 2024" (CORR.md later changes that to 20 July 2024). No document cites an adopting implementing regulation or its date.

The files do not name a notified body for the MA STAR two post lift. The MAHA operating instructions (BA364501-en, section 10, Declaration of Conformity, p. 37) list the directives, the standards and a 'Person Authorised to Compile the Technical File' (Ralf Kerkmeier), but no notified body or type-examination certificate. The plant records (IGEA scheda tecnica) do not mention the MA STAR.

The files do not contain the EC declaration of conformity for the complete robot cell. The only declarations for the UR5e and UR10e arms are the manufacturer's EU Declaration of Incorporation in each user manual (ur5e-manual.md and ur10e-manual.md, Section 20.1, pp. 220 and 227), dated Odense, 20 December 2024. That declaration covers the partly completed machine, not the final cell, and says the integrator must issue the Declaration of Conformity for the complete machine.

Under Article 54 (Entry into force and application) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Article 50(1) on Member States' duty to lay down penalties applies from 14 October 2023, ahead of the general application date of 14 January 2027. Article 50(2), the notification duty, is a separate obligation with a 14 October 2026 deadline.

Under Article 54, point (a), of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Articles 26 to 42 (including the notification of conformity assessment bodies) apply from 14 January 2024. The corrigendum (CORR.md, point 11) corrects that date to 20 January 2024.

Under Article 6(9) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Member States must first provide the Article 6(5) data and information by 14 July 2025, and every five years after that. The corrigendum (CORR.md, page 17) changed that date to 20 July 2025.

Under Article 53(1) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (REG.md, 'Art. 53(1)'), the Commission must submit its first report on the evaluation and review of the Regulation to the European Parliament and the Council by 14 July 2028, and every four years after that.

Yes. Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Article 51(2), repeals Directive 2006/42/EC with effect from 14 January 2027, but the corrigendum (CORR.md, point 5) changes that date to 20 January 2027. Since 18 January 2027 falls before that date, the Directive is still in force on that day.

Yes. Under Article 54(b) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (REG.md), Article 50(1) on penalties applies from 14 October 2023, so it already applied on 1 September 2026, well before the general application date of 14 January 2027. The 14 October 2026 date in Article 50(2) is for notifying the Commission of the rules, not for applying Article 50(1).

No. Under Article 52(1) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Chapter VI was to apply from 13 July 2023 to products placed on the market under Directive 2006/42/EC. The OJ corrigendum (L 169, 4.7.2023, point 7) changed that date to 19 July 2023, so on 15 July 2023 Chapter VI did not yet apply.

Yes. Under Article 52(1) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, as corrected by the corrigendum, Member States may not impede making available on the market products placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC before 20 January 2027. The machine was placed on the market on 15 January 2027, which is before that corrected date, so it is covered on 1 March 2027. The uncorrected text in REG.md says 14 January 2027, which would exclude it.

Yes. Under DM 2011 art. 2, c. 1, the ASL holds the periodic verifications after the first, due within 30 days of the request. Under Allegato II, punto 5.2.1, the employer must request that ASL at least 30 days before the deadline. Art. 2, c. 8 allows the employer to use an authorised body only after the c. 1 terms have elapsed.

Yes. Article 71, paragraph 13-bis of Legislative Decree 81/2008, which the Ministerial Decree of 11 April 2011 implements, allows the Corpo nazionale dei vigili del fuoco to carry out the periodic verifications itself for equipment in Annex VII that it holds as owner or on loan for use. The aerial ladder falls under Annex VII group SP ('Scale aeree ad inclinazione variabile', DM2011 Allegato II, point 1.1.2a), so the brigade may verify it directly. The DM2011 text itself does not contain this exception.

Under Article 52(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (REG.md), EC type-examination certificates and approval decisions issued under Article 12 of Directive 2006/42/EC remain valid until they expire; the files give no fixed end date. The Directive is repealed with effect from 14 January 2027 (Article 51(2)).

Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (REG.md), Article 6(11), says the Commission shall adopt the delegated acts 'if necessary after the Commission report referred to in Article 53(3)', but it sets no date by which they must be adopted. Article 47(2) only gives the Commission the power to adopt delegated acts under Articles 6(2), 6(11) and 7(2) for five years from 13 July 2023, which is a period of delegated power, not an adoption deadline.

Article 71(14) of Legislative Decree 81/2008 (DLGS71.md, section 'art. 71, c. 14') sets no deadline for adopting the ministerial decree amending Annex VII. The only time limit in Article 71 is the twelve months in paragraph 13, which concerns the decree on how periodic inspections are carried out, not the Annex VII list amendment.
